metadata.title: The Well-Tempered clAIvier
metadata.subtitle: IV. Prelude in C-sharp minor
composition_notes: Original 32-bar prelude, composed explicitly in three monophonic layers.
The rising fifth and semitone upper neighbor anticipate Fugue IV.
E-major cantabile gives way to a sixteenth-note current and an A-major deceptive arrival.
D-major over F-sharp supplies the Neapolitan color in bars 23 and 29.
The final tonic remains minor, reserving the fugue's brighter final third.
This free prelude is not represented as a strict-species contrapuntal exercise.

second_edition.review: The explicitly composed melodic and harmonic design is retained; a register-reset approach to the high return is repaired, and phrase-level dynamics/articulation are clarified.

changes.reason: Prepare the high return by a fifth, not a 17-semitone leap.

performance_revision.description: Deterministic subject/countersubject balance, phrase arches, metrical articulation, connected suspensions, cadence release and keyboard-register stereo placement.
performance_revision.timing: No onset displacement, random timing, tempo changes, or written-duration changes.
performance_revision.soundfont: FluidR3_GM.sf2 General MIDI study samples; not an acoustic performance.
